title: AI chip startup Salience Labs raises $125m for work to tackle data centre energy issues
key_facts: Oxford-based Salience Labs raised $125m (£94m) in a Series B led by Bullhound Capital.
Investors include AMD Ventures, Intel Capital, SBI Group, Hudson River Trading and the British Business Bank.
It makes photonic chips that move data as light, with optical circuit switching to cut power use and delays.
The money will scale manufacturing and its Silicon Valley presence.
UK grid connection queue tripled from 41 GW to 125 GW between Nov 2024 and Jun 2025, per an Ofgem consultation.
CEO Vaysh Kewada: "OCS will play a critical role in AI datacenter networking".
quote_evidence: Oxford-based chip startup Salience Labs has secured $125m (£94m) from a group of high-profile investors, including Intel and AMD, as the scramble to construct AI data centres places mounting strain on power grids.
"OCS will play a critical role in AI datacenter networking", said Vaysh Kewada, chief executive and co-founder of Salience Labs.
why_it_matters_hint: Light-based switching is pitched as a way to let data centres spend more of scarce power on AI itself.
notes: Business Live credits City AM; City AM original not read.
